# The Right Area in Every Language

Version 1.7.5 is a fix release: the NINA area chip is clean whatever language your Home Assistant server speaks, renamed DWD sensors are found again, and AI translation sends fewer requests.

## Fixes

- **The NINA area chip shows the area in every server language.** With `show_nina_area` the card read the area from the warning entity's name and could only strip the English "Warning" and the German "Warnung". On a server set to another language, for example Dutch, the chip read "Aachen, Stadt (Aachen, Städteregion - Nordrhein-Westfalen) Waarschuwing", and the district part was not shortened either. The card now takes the area from the NINA device, which is named after the area in every language, so the chip reads "Aachen, Stadt" with the full name in the tooltip. The area dropdown in the editor uses the same name. If you renamed a NINA device, the chip shows your name. Thanks to the user who reported this in the [forum](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/lovelace-nina-and-dwd-warnings-card/943706/7). _[#106]_
- **Renamed DWD sensors are found again.** With `dwd_device` set, the card looked for the current and advance warning sensors by the end of their entity id, such as `_current_warning_level` or `_vorwarnstufe`. After renaming one, for example to `sensor.dwd_home_current`, the card showed a green "No Warnings" while a warning was active. It now recognises the sensors by the key the DWD integration gives them, and still falls back to the entity id. The suggested configuration when you add the card works the same way. _[#105]_
- **AI translation only translates the warnings on the card.** With `enable_translation`, every collected warning was sent to your AI Task entity, including those that `hide_on_level_below`, `max_warnings` or the merging of duplicates keep off the card. Each of them was a request your AI provider may charge for. Only the warnings the card shows are translated now. _[#105]_
- **Several cards keep each other's translations.** Each card kept its own copy of the translation cache and wrote it back whole, so with two cards on one dashboard the second card dropped the first card's translations, and they were requested again after every reload. All cards now share one cache. _[#105]_

## Upgrading

Nothing to do after updating; refresh the browser cache so the new `nina-dwd-card.js` is loaded. If you use `show_nina_area` with English or German as server language, the chips look as before unless you renamed a NINA device.
